question: Can source-learned uncertainty about head sharing preserve the joint archive benefit while permitting eta to escape an f/g-compatible archive?
core: Keep the source-learned risk covariance atoms and per-archive risk/full reference unchanged. Add a latent shared versus separate archive identity for eta and f/g. Shared has the A27 joint evidence. Separate has p(f/g past) times p(eta past) using the same source archive pool. A prior on sharing is updated only by source calibration and target prefixes; no hard switch based on detected regime or generator metadata.
primary_reference: Uniform Beta(1,1) sharing probability, integrated before any source empirical update. Retain the sharing posterior and coefficient-mixture uncertainty. Compare against unchanged J and A, without promoting a secondary model from target outcomes.
phase_1: Source-only reference-prior validation on the original eight held seed pairs, both matched and co-shift conditions. Recover the same small f/g moment priors and raw component prefix evidence once. Preserve all source losses, including compatible loss if the extra uncertainty is costly. No target records are inputs.
phase_2: If source calibration is justified by phase1, freeze it separately before fitting. Any outer held-pair calibration must also exclude that pair from the population priors used in its training scores: cache per-archive evidence and remove both outer-held and inner-scored pair columns. Do not calibrate on meta-priors that already contain held-archive parameters.
risk_only_stress: A source-only optional diagnostic can recombine f/g records from one existing archive with eta records from its fixed partner, using their own observed input banks and noises. This is a cross-head record stress, not a co-observed physical simulator task, not new data and not an estimated deployment frequency. Freeze its weight separately before using it in any calibration; never claim it independently confirms target risk-only performance.
high_frequency_scope: Sharing uncertainty cannot be assumed to repair directions missing from all source risk covariances. Keep the A28 generic full-risk reference and high-frequency negative result. A risk covariance/family-discrepancy update is a separate later one-variable study, not combined with the sharing modification.
analysis: All pair-block source strata, early9-12/late21-24, joint versus eta-only posterior sharing and risk-family masses. Eight-block nominal bootstrap. No target-driven q, weight floors or winning-branch selection.
resource_admission: Retain source priors and first complete component-evidence path; project complete256-path source coverage with1.25 safety factor and20 CPU seconds summary reserve. Cache Gaussian prefix evidence once and reuse branch/sharing computations. Stop on projected90-CPU-second excess.
gate: Reference-prior/source-calibration evidence must be reviewed before freezing any target test. No target study, recommendation replay or new search follows automatically.
limitations: The original source archives do not contain naturally co-observed risk-only structural shifts. Sharing frequency for such deployment shifts cannot be identified merely from shared/co-shift panels. More source information, finite empirical covariance atoms and noise-model assumptions remain explicit.

implementation_fixed_before_run.retained_cache: Per-archive prefix evidence is kept for all32 archives; each issued prediction drops both held seeds except its explicit local prior. Subsequent nested calibration can drop outer-held pair columns as well without repeating Gaussian inference.
implementation_fixed_before_run.sharing_state_vs_parameter: A uniform Beta prior integrates to shared-state prior1/2. The posterior shared-state probability is distinct from the continuous sharing-probability mean: E[q|data]=(1+P(shared|data))/3 under the reference.
